source.title: Handler beliefs affect scent detection dog outcomes

confidence_rationale: This is the strongest modern, peer-reviewed, controlled replication of the Clever Hans effect in a working-animal paradigm, and it is directly on-point for the source thought's 'Blind' workflow step: it shows human belief about a condition contaminates the interpretation of animal behavioral output even when the animal's actual behavior is unaffected by the (absent) target stimulus. It both supports the thought's instinct that blinding matters AND complicates the specific proposed implementation, because the contamination here occurred in a live, in-the-loop human-animal interaction, not in after-the-fact scoring of pre-recorded trajectories -- a distinction the source thought's 'Blind' step (hide condition labels during scoring) does not fully address. Confidence held at 0.55 because REE's Fishtank trajectories are generated by a fixed environment/policy with no live human 'handler' present during generation, so the closest REE analogue is the human researcher's own visual impression-formation, a narrower target than the paper's live-interaction paradigm.
failure_signatures: Handlers were falsely told scent-target markers were present at certain search locations. Across 164 search trials with NO drug or explosive scent actually present anywhere, handlers reported 225 dog alerts, disproportionately at the falsely marked locations -- human belief manufactured the appearance of correct animal behavioral output where none of the eliciting stimulus existed.

Human influence on alert location outweighed dog-directed decoy influence (food/toy placed to independently attract the dog) in the same design, showing the contamination pathway ran primarily through the human interpreter/handler, not through the animal's own behavior -- i.e. blinding the SCORER after the fact would not have caught this, because the bias entered during data GENERATION via the handler's real-time interpretation and cuing, not during a separate post-hoc analysis step.

mapping.source_claim_statement: 18 trained drug/explosive detection dog-handler teams ran search scenarios in which handlers were given false beliefs about scent-marker locations (human-directed bias) and separate decoys were placed to attract the dog independently (dog-directed bias), with no actual target scent present in any condition. Handler false beliefs produced substantially more false alert reports at the falsely-marked locations than at unmarked ones, and human influence exceeded dog influence in a formal comparison.
mapping.ree_translation: GOV-BEHADJ-1's 'Blind' step proposes hiding condition labels during behavioral SCORING. This paper shows that in a live paradigm, the point of contamination was earlier -- during the human's real-time interpretation of, and interaction with, the animal's behavior -- which a post-hoc scoring blind alone would not fully guard against. For REE, the closest structural analogue is not the (already blind, since generated by a fixed policy with no live human observer) Fishtank run itself, but the RESEARCHER'S initial visual impression of a trajectory ('post-sleep behaviour looked smoother') that seeds the hypothesis before any formal blinded scoring occurs. This paper is evidence that such an unblinded first look, even by a careful observer with no intent to bias the outcome, is a documented, quantitatively substantial source of false structure detection in a formally analogous animal-behavior-interpretation task, reinforcing the source thought's own caution: 'An observation may generate a hypothesis, but it does not confirm itself.'
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's paradigm involves a LIVE human-animal dyad with real-time interaction (handler cuing the dog, consciously or not, during the search) -- REE's Fishtank agent generates a trajectory with no human present, so the specific cuing mechanism (subtle handler movement/tension) has no REE analogue. The transferable finding is narrower: human belief about condition can distort INTERPRETATION of behavioral output independent of whether the belief-holder is influencing the behavior itself, which is the risk relevant to a REE researcher's initial visual read of a trajectory, not to trajectory generation.
mapping.source_context: 18 professional drug/explosive detection dog-handler teams, 4 search scenarios each in 2 sessions, no actual target scent present in any trial, handler beliefs and independent dog-directed decoys manipulated factorially.

confidence_components.notes: Well-designed, peer-reviewed, widely cited controlled study with a clear factorial manipulation and a striking effect size (225 false alerts across 164 no-scent trials). Mapping fidelity held down because the live-interaction cuing mechanism central to the paper's finding has no direct REE analogue; what transfers is the more general point about unblinded belief contaminating interpretation, which is real but less specific.
